caption: Fig. 9. The overall architecture of HNLPU system. (a) System-level architecture of HNLPU, featuring a logical 4×4 row-column fully-connected fabric to interconnect its 16 modules. (b) Architecture of a single compute module, comprising the core die and HBM.

templates.why_chosen: (a) a 4x4 fully connected chip mesh, (b) one chip enlarged - topology and node internals in one figure.
templates.what_to_learn: For mesh/topology figures, panel (a) is the graph and panel (b) is a dashed-connected zoom of a single node; the shared HBM bar spans the bottom of (b).

templates.why_chosen: A 4x4 chip-mesh topology overview (a) is joined by a dashed leader to a zoomed single-chip block diagram (b), the overview-with-inset-inside-composite pattern, with the zoom revealing the Control Unit/HN Array/VEX/Buffer stack over shared HBM.
templates.what_to_learn: Zoom a dashed leader from one node in a repeated mesh topology into a single expanded block diagram rather than drawing every node's internals, and spell out abbreviated module names in full (this figure's 'Inter. Engine' is ambiguous without the caption, a listed weakness) so the inset stands on its own.

templates.why_chosen: High-confidence rank-18 canonical floorplan: Control Unit sits in a top corner, HN Array fills the compute middle, and one HBM bar spans the full width below, paired with a 4x4 fully-connected chip-mesh overview.
templates.what_to_learn: Place control in a top corner, compute in the middle, and let one memory bar span the full width along the bottom edge exactly as the rule prescribes, then pair the single-chip floorplan with a system-level mesh panel joined by one dashed zoom leader rather than expanding all sixteen chips.
